## Background 
For this report, we compare IQ scores between children who lived near a lead-emitting ore smelter and those who lived farther away. The dataset includes and observation of 124 children between the ages of 3 and 15 in El Paso, Texas. Location is recorded as Near for children who lived within one mile of the smelter and Far for those who lived farther away. IQ was measured using the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children.
Although we are comparing IQ by location, the original study compared children with high and low lead levels. Any differences observed here describe the two location groups and do not establish that living near the smelter caused a difference in IQ.

## Data Import and inspect 

```{r import-data}
lead <- read.csv("../DataRaw/lead-iq-01.csv")

names(lead)
head(lead)
str(lead)

```

##Data Correction 
After a brief conversation with the primary investigator, we find out one individual who had an IQ value of “999” was in fact supposed to have a value of “99”. Thus the change was made. 
```{r}
lead$IQ[lead$IQ == 999] <- 99
```


## IQ Levels by Location

```{r}
boxplot(IQ ~ Smelter,
   data = lead,
   main = "IQ Levels by Location Status",
   xlab = "Location", ylab = "IQ Score",
   col = c("lightblue", "lightgreen"))
```

The boxplot compares IQ scores between children who lived near the smelter and those who lived farther away. The Far group has a higher median IQ.

## Summary Table of IQ Scores

```{r iq-summary}
iq_summary <- t(sapply(
  split(lead$IQ, lead$Smelter),
  function(x) c(N = length(x), Mean = mean(x),
                SD = sd(x), Median = median(x))
))

knitr::kable(iq_summary, digits = 2,
             caption = "IQ scores by location status")
```

The table summarizes the number of children, mean, standard
deviation, and median IQ for each location group. The mean IQ
was `r round(iq_summary["Far", "Mean"], 2)` in the Far group
and `r round(iq_summary["Near", "Mean"], 2)` in the Near group.
